Write a RED script under packages/main/tests/red/ proving the fixture fails on current main, then fix the fixture to stub both files, confirm GREEN.

edge.desc: Deliberately reverting the stub-content fix reproduces the original snapshot_missing failure, proving the fixture still discriminates a real regression

adversarial.desc: Stub content for the two new files is not merely trivial-pass filler -- it mirrors the shape/role of the real files closely enough that the snapshot closure genuinely reflects the real registry entrys structure, not a shortcut that would also mask a different future regression

items.title: Fix field-regression-cli-smoke.ts missing --readManifest + stale assertion pattern (RED then GREEN)
items.context: assertReviewRunStartCliSurface calls review_pass_set without the now-required --readManifest argument (command-catalog.ts), so the real error is an argument-validation failure, not the /already stale|stale/i pattern the fixture own assertion expects. Write a RED script proving the current mismatch, then fix the fixture to pass a valid readManifest matching the shape other passing tests use so it actually exercises the staleness scenario, confirm GREEN.

happy.desc: RED script red-B-74b9-chk002-readmanifest.mjs fails on the pre-fix tree with the readManifest argument-validation mismatch signature

edge.desc: The fixed fixture actual assertion genuinely matches an already-stale review_pass_set response, not merely a non-crashing one -- confirmed by inspecting the real CLI output the test asserts against

adversarial.desc: Confirm the readManifest object passed is NOT so permissive/empty that it would also silently pass if the staleness detection itself were broken -- it must contain a plausible non-empty filesReadFully/filesTriagedByName shape matching real reviewer usage

items.userSees: node packages/main/dist/tasks/field-regression-cli-smoke.js prints its pass output and exits 0 (no readManifest argument-validation error).

items.title: Fix worktree-authority-smoke.ts done_recover post-merge version-bump ENOENT (RED then GREEN)
items.context: assertDoneRecoverRunsPostMergeBuildForRuntimeChanges's synthetic mkdtemp root has no package.json, but done_recover now also runs bumpVersionOnDoneMerge (core/version-bump.ts) which requires root/package.json and the other version sync points to exist, throwing ENOENT before the stubbed build runner is ever reached. Write a RED script proving the current ENOENT, then fix the fixture's root scaffold to include the version sync-point files done_recover's post-merge path now needs, confirm GREEN.

happy.desc: RED script red-B-74b9-chk003-version-bump.mjs fails on the pre-fix tree with the ENOENT package.json signature

A fresh run of worktree-authority-smoke.js no longer contains the DONE post-merge version bump failed / ENOENT package.json signature (confirmed via a dedicated grep-style check). NOTE: the whole file still exits non-zero after this fix, but now ONLY due to a confirmed-unrelated, separately-tracked pre-existing bug (task_a8d49518, assertConcurrentDoneSerializesWithoutPartialDone, a concurrent DONE-lock race unmasked by fixing this ENOENT crash that used to abort the script earlier) -- verified via isolated reproduction on a clean untouched main checkout before being excluded from this items scope.

edge.desc: Investigation confirmed a fixture-only fix suffices: bumpVersionOnDoneMerge/applyPatchBump reads package.json etc. from the filesystem via readFileSync (not git history), and every real Proofbound repo root always has these files by construction -- the ENOENT can only occur in a synthetic fixture root, never in real partial-DONE recovery

adversarial.desc: Confirmed bumpVersionOnDoneMerge already assumes package.json always exists on any real repo root (readSyncedVersion/applyPatchBump read all 5 sync-point files unconditionally via readFileSync); the ENOENT truly cannot occur on a genuine partial-DONE recovery, only on a synthetic fixture that never had these files -- the fixture-only fix does not mask a real production gap

items.userSees: node packages/main/dist/tasks/worktree-authority-smoke.js prints its pass output and exits 0 (no ENOENT package.json error).

items.title: Decide and record whether the three fixed fixtures should be registered in lattice.config.json validate.commands
items.context: All three fixtures currently run only via the broader root npm test, not lattice validate. After fixing them, decide per-fixture whether they should be added to validate.commands so lattice validate (and REVIEW rounds relying on it) catches this class of regression going forward, and record the reasoning in background.md or plan.md.

happy.desc: plan.md (or background.md) records an explicit per-fixture registration decision for validate.commands and/or test:serial-reference, with rationale, correcting the earlier confirmed-inaccurate assumption that these were already covered by root npm test

edge.desc: If a fixture is newly registered into validate.commands and/or test:serial-reference, the corresponding aggregate command (lattice validate and/or root npm test) still completes cleanly afterward with no new flakiness/timeout

adversarial.desc: The decision is not a default blanket register-all-or-register-none -- each of the three fixtures gets an independent, justified decision referencing its own runtime/isolation profile

items.userSees: plan.md or background.md contains a clearly labeled per-fixture validate.commands/test:serial-reference registration decision with rationale for each of the three fixtures.
